title: token-level-observability: cost/latency dashboards and alert tuning
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: provide token-level visibility for cost and latency across serving routes and model variants, and add tuned alerts to catch regressions earlier. This PR builds on previous token-level work (see ENG-2043/ENG-2178) and consolidates dashboards + alert rules used during the recent canary runs.

This change adds: 1) new Grafana dashboard json for Token Cost / Latency breakdown per-route and per-model-variant, 2) additional metrics emitted from the runtime: token_latency_seconds_bucketed, token_cost_usd_total (labels: route, model, variant, backend_pool), kv_cache_hit_ratio per-request, 3) tracing link enrichment to correlate slow tokens with upstream model variant fallbacks, 4) tuned alert rules: P99 token latency regression, sustained token-cost increase (>10% 30m window), low KV cache hit ratio per-route, 5) README updates and migration notes for SRE and on-call.

Checklist:
- [x] runtime metric instrumentation (token-level metrics)
- [x] grafana dashboard panels + templating (route/model)
- [x] alert rules + test alerts in staging
- [x] docs + migration notes
- [x] unit + integration tests for metric emitters

Notes:
- Metrics are exported via the existing Prometheus exporter and use the same scrape path (/metrics). No changes to prometheus config required aside from adding the new alert rules file to the prometheus server config in deploy manifests (included in this PR).
- Alerts were tuned after two days of staging traffic; thresholds are conservative (10%+ regression windows) to reduce noise. We expect to iterate once on-call feedback arrives.
- Small schema change: token_cost_usd_total is a cumulative counter; cost calculation uses existing token pricing config (no new credentials).

Related: Linear ENG-4521, ENG-4689. Linked docs: ./docs/observability/token-metrics.md

review_comments: Ravi Shah: Overall LGTM. A couple of questions: 1) Are the P99 thresholds derived from historical baselines or fixed numbers? 2) Can we avoid adding high-cardinality labels to token_cost_usd_total?

Ava Martinez: Answered - thresholds were derived from the last 14 days of staging traffic (script in tests). token_cost_usd_total keeps labels to route/model/variant only, not request_id or user_id. I also added a note in token-metrics.md about cardinality guidance.
Katherine Wu: Suggest pulling kv_cache_hit_ratio into a derived per-route 5m avg for alerts to reduce flapping. Also flagged a minor race in prometheus_exporter reconcilers.
Ava Martinez: Implemented 5m avg in alert rules and fixed reconciling race (prometheus_exporter.go line ~142). Pushed the fix in commit 'fix(exporter): reconcile race for metric registration'.
Ben Carter: Ran staging canary. Alerts fired as expected for the injected regression test. Approving once CI completes and we confirm no Prometheus scrape errors in prod rollout.
